forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329120647_c4ea7dea
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Set I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}, and let R := Q[x_s : s in I] be the polynomial ring graded by deg(x_s) = s for each s in I. For each positive integer d define M_d(u,v) := |{m in Z : u < m <= v and d divides m}|. Assume M_d(r+a, r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d. Then there exists a family (f_s)_{s in I} of homogeneous polynomials in R such that deg(f_s) = r+s for every s in I, and the ordered list of these polynomials in increasing order of s is a regular sequence in R. If I is empty, this means the empty family.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329110006_654a633e
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r, j be integers with 0 <= a <= b, r >= 0, and 0 <= j <= floor(r (b - a) / 2). Put I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}. For each positive integer d, define M_d(u,v) := |{m in Z : u < m <= v and d divides m}|, and assume M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d. Let X_j be the set of pairs (S, lambda) such that S is a subset of I, lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I, |lambda| denotes the sum of the elements of lambda, and |lambda| + sum_{s in S} (r + s) = j. Then there exists an involution iota_j : X_j -> X_j such that: (1) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S',lambda') != (S,lambda), then |S'| is congruent to |S| + 1 modulo 2; and (2) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S,lambda), then |S| is even.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329092547_6a64d34a
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: For integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, let q be an indeterminate, define (q;q)_n := product_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j) for n >= 0 with (q;q)_0 := 1, set R_{a,b,r}(q) := ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b), and define D := r (b - a). Assume that R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q]. Then for every integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), the coefficient of q^j in R_{a,b,r}(q) is a nonnegative integer.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329074016_d9949d95
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Define P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), with empty product equal to 1. Assume that for every positive integer d one has floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d) >= floor(b/d) - floor(a/d). Then P_{a,b,r}(q) is a polynomial in Z[q], and every coefficient of P_{a,b,r}(q) is nonnegative.

payload.statement_nl: Let a and b be integers with 0 <= a <= b. Put I := {a+1,...,b}, let S := Q[y_1,...,y_b] with weighted grading deg(y_i)=i, and let R := Q[x_s : s in I] with weighted grading deg(x_s)=s. Then the quotient S/(y_1,...,y_a) is canonically isomorphic to R as a graded Q-algebra, via the map sending the class of y_s to x_s for each s in I. Under this graded isomorphism, homogeneous regular sequences correspond and weighted degrees are preserved. When a=b, both rings are Q.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Let J := (y_1,...,y_a) be the ideal of S, and put A := S/J. Because each y_i is homogeneous of weighted degree i, the ideal J is homogeneous, so A inherits the quotient weighted grading.

Define a Q-algebra homomorphism theta : S -> R by theta(y_i)=0 for 1 <= i <= a and theta(y_s)=x_s for s in I={a+1,...,b}. Since theta(y_i)=0 for i<=a, we have J subset ker(theta), so theta descends uniquely to a Q-algebra homomorphism theta_bar : A -> R. By construction, theta_bar(y_s+J)=x_s for every s in I.

Conversely, define a Q-algebra homomorphism psi : R -> A by psi(x_s)=y_s+J for s in I. Then, for every s in I,
(theta_bar o psi)(x_s)=theta_bar(y_s+J)=x_s,
so theta_bar o psi = id_R because the x_s generate R as a Q-algebra. Also, for i<=a we have y_i+J=0 in A, hence (psi o theta_bar)(y_i+J)=0=y_i+J, and for s in I we have
(psi o theta_bar)(y_s+J)=psi(x_s)=y_s+J.
Since the classes y_1+J,...,y_b+J generate A as a Q-algebra, psi o theta_bar = id_A. Therefore theta_bar is an isomorphism A -> R. It is canonical: there is only one Q-algebra map A -> R sending the class of y_s to x_s for s in I, because A is generated by the classes of y_1,...,y_b and the first a of those classes are already 0.

This isomorphism is graded. Indeed, y_i+J=0 for i<=a, so A is generated as a Q-algebra by the homogeneous elements y_s+J for s in I. A monomial product over s in I of (y_s+J)^{e_s} has weighted degree sum_s s e_s, and theta_bar sends it to the monomial product over s in I of x_s^{e_s}, which has the same weighted degree. Hence theta_bar(A_d) subset R_d for every d. The same argument with psi shows psi(R_d) subset A_d for every d. Thus theta_bar is a graded Q-algebra isomorphism, so weighted degrees of homogeneous elements are preserved.

Now let f_1,...,f_m be homogeneous elements of A, and put g_i := theta_bar(f_i) in R. Then each g_i is homogeneous of the same weighted degree as f_i. For each r with 0 <= r < m, the isomorphism theta_bar carries the ideal (f_1,...,f_r) onto the ideal (g_1,...,g_r), so it induces a ring isomorphism A/(f_1,...,f_r) -> R/(g_1,...,g_r). Under this induced isomorphism, multiplication by the class of f_{r+1} corresponds exactly to multiplication by the class of g_{r+1}. Therefore multiplication by f_{r+1} on A/(f_1,...,f_r) is injective if and only if multiplication by g_{r+1} on R/(g_1,...,g_r) is injective. Equivalently, f_{r+1} is a non-zero-divisor modulo (f_1,...,f_r) if and only if g_{r+1} is a non-zero-divisor modulo (g_1,...,g_r). Hence f_1,...,f_m is a regular sequence if and only if g_1,...,g_m is a regular sequence. If one includes the usual extra requirement that the generated ideal be proper (or that the successive quotients be nonzero), that is also preserved by the same quotient-ring isomorphisms. So homogeneous regular sequences correspond under theta_bar.

Finally, if a=b, then I is empty, so R = Q[x_s : s in empty set] = Q. Also A = S/(y_1,...,y_b) = Q[y_1,...,y_b]/(y_1,...,y_b) = Q. Thus when a=b, both rings are Q, as claimed.
result_payload.proof_summary: Let J=(y_1,...,y_a). Define theta:S->R by killing y_1,...,y_a and sending y_s to x_s for s>a; it factors through A=S/J. Define psi:R->A by x_s↦y_s+J. These maps are inverse Q-algebra homomorphisms, so A and R are canonically isomorphic. Because surviving generators keep the same weighted degrees, the isomorphism is graded and preserves degrees. Any ring isomorphism induces isomorphisms on quotients by corresponding ideals, so the non-zero-divisor condition in the definition of regular sequence is preserved in both directions; hence homogeneous regular sequences correspond. When a=b, both sides are Q.
